title: rEngine project declaration, contracts 1 through 9
description: Read from <root>/.rengine/project.json. Contract 1 declares file formats whose previews are produced by the project's own executables (docs/specs/074-project-format-registry.md); contract 2 adds an optional dashboard of grouped actions (docs/specs/075-project-dashboard.md); contract 3 adds an optional array of games the workspace launches (docs/specs/078-project-game-declaration.md); contract 4 adds an optional array of devices saying where each target runs, and an optional device on a game record and a dashboard action (docs/specs/082-project-devices.md). Cross-field rules the service also enforces: default is one of modes; preview is required when modes contains preview; a preview command names ${file}; an entry command names ${file} and ${entry}; format ids are unique; dashboard requires contract 2, games requires contract 3, and devices or any device key requires contract 4; group, action, game and device ids are unique; an action carries only its kind's fields; a game action's game names a declared games record and its args are literal argv without placeholders; a device reference names a declared device or the implicit local; a game whose surface is embedded or cooperative streams into a local pane and so binds to the local device; local is a reserved id/kind pairing that takes no probe, host or selector; host and selector each carry exactly one of value or env; a probe placeholder must have a declared source; script/requires/artifacts/into are root-relative and requires stays local even on a remote device; dashboard env keys are UPPER_SNAKE; game env keys are UPPER_SNAKE and never start with RENGINE_, DYLD_ or LD_; game requires entries and game cwd are root-relative. Contract 5 adds an optional display title and an icon of a glyph plus a design token name, which the workspace chrome and the window title wear in place of their defaults. It also adds an optional tracker naming where the project's task list lives, whose repository, team, inventory, project, assignee and states keys each belong to one provider and are refused under the others (docs/specs/083-task-tracking.md, docs/specs/100-tracker-view-filters.md). Contract 6 adds an optional tracker.write naming the project's own command that writes one task row (literal argv naming ${json}; local provider only), and an optional top-level agents array saying which agent CLIs and models this project offers when an agent is spawned on a task (docs/specs/103-task-driven-agents.md). Cross-field rules for it: write belongs to provider local, one of its arguments must name ${json}, each agents record's default must be one of its models, and agent cli ids are unique. Contract 7 adds an optional languageServers array naming the language servers this project's files are served by (docs/specs/102-editor-as-claude-ide.md). Contract 8 adds brand artwork: an icon.image rasterised into the mark chip in place of its glyph, and a wordmark drawn in place of the title text, either one file or a light/dark pair (docs/specs/104-project-brand-artwork.md). Cross-field rules for it: icon carries exactly one of glyph and image; image and wordmark paths are declaration-relative and refused when they escape; both require contract 8. Contract 9 adds an optional packs array: one pinned, versioned artifact per entry (docs/specs/107-pack-manifest.md, charter D39). Each pack carries a name, a pin of a spoken version and a checked 40- or 64-character hex revision, and facets saying how it is consumed: a library facet of a root-relative path and a CMake target a game consumes at build time, a plugin facet of a root-relative module and an opaque abi string the editor loads at run time, or both. Cross-field rules for it: a pack declares at least one facet; pack names are unique; a facet key under the wrong facet is refused by the facet it belongs to; poweredBy was removed by charter D45 and is refused on either facet, because an adoption is recorded by the owner's sign-off in a spec rather than claimed in a declaration (docs/specs/112-poweredby-removed.md); a revision that is a branch, a tag or a short prefix is refused by name; library.path and plugin.module are root-relative. A pack is DECLARED, never acquired: this contract carries no URL, registry or fetch step, and the reader opens neither path, because licence, distribution and packaging are open (KI-008) and the boundary forbids hidden downloads.

games.description: Games this project can launch, in declaration order. Declaring games requires contract 3, so a reader that predates it answers "unknown contract" instead of "unknown key". An omitted gameId on the preflight/launch routes selects the first record.

devices.description: Devices this project's targets run on, in declaration order. Declaring devices requires contract 4, so a reader that predates it answers "unknown contract" instead of "unknown key". The id "local" is reserved for this machine and is implicit: a target without a device binds to it.

title.description: Display name shown in the workspace chrome and the window title. Never an identifier: `project` stays the stable identity used for binding and paths.

icon.description: The brand mark. Either a short glyph on a colour named from the design tokens, so the letter's contrast is a property of the theme rather than a per-project accident, or artwork the chrome rasterises in place of both (contract 8). Exactly one of glyph and image.

glyph.description: One or two characters; the chip is a fixed square.

token.description: A design token name such as accent, ok, warn, err or info. Resolved against the live preset.

image.description: contract 8: an SVG rasterised into the mark chip, replacing the glyph and its token fill. Declaration-relative, so an external declaration resolves beside itself rather than inside the root.

tracker.description: Where this project's task list lives. Read-only in the workspace: the view lists and opens, it never writes. Carries no credential — a provider token is read from the workspace state directory, which is not committed.

provider.description: local reads the project's own features.json directly, deriving the same readiness rule tools/features.py applies; github reads repository issues; linear reads a team's issues.

team.description: linear only: the team key, such as KOH.

inventory.description: local only: path to the inventory within the root; defaults to features.json.

project.description: linear only: narrow the team's issues to one project by name. A team without this shows everything it holds, which is rarely what a person opening one project wants.

assignee.description: linear only: narrow to one person. "me" is the signed-in user, whoever the token belongs to; any other value is matched against Linear's displayName. A project still holds everyone's work, and a person opening their own workspace wants their own.

states.description: linear only: narrow to these workflow-state categories, which is the vocabulary the neutral row normalises to rather than a team's own state names, so the declaration says the same word the row shows. Omitted shows every state.

write.description: local only, contract 6: the project's own command that writes one task row, as literal argv with no shell. One argument must name ${json}, which is replaced by the JSON document the workspace sends: the row's fields plus the action (add, update or decompose) and, for a child row, its parent. The workspace never edits the inventory text itself; this command is the validated path the project already trusts.

agents.description: Contract 6: the agent CLIs and models this project offers when an agent is spawned on a task, in declaration order. Absent, the menu is the CLIs rEngine can launch with its own known model lists. Declaring it requires contract 6, so a reader that predates it answers "unknown contract" instead of "unknown key".

languageServers.description: Contract 7: the language servers this project's files are served by. rEngine runs a declared server, it never installs one, and an undeclared project answers an empty diagnostic list rather than guessing. Declaring it requires contract 7, so a reader that predates it answers "unknown contract" instead of "unknown key".

wordmark.description: contract 8: artwork the chrome draws in place of the title text. A string is used on every theme; a light/dark pair lets a wordmark of ink invert with the ground. `title` remains required for identity either way — the OS window title is a string and no image can reach it.

packs.description: Contract 9: the packs this project stands on — the library packs its build consumes and the plugins the editor loads for it, in one list because a pack is one concept (charter D39, docs/specs/107-pack-manifest.md). Declaring it requires contract 9, so a reader that predates it answers "unknown contract" instead of "unknown key".

argument.description: A literal argv element; the only placeholders are ${file} and ${entry}.

executable.description: argv[0]: absolute, project-relative with a separator, or a bare PATH name. Never a shell expression.

title.description: Titles are drawn as text in the desktop's own faces: a glyph the installed faces lack falls back to another loaded face and then to a small substitution table, so a symbol outside that set draws as a box. Expect the fallback rather than relying on it; a guaranteed symbol needs an icon, not text.

items.description: Case-insensitive shell glob on the file name (*, ?, [...]).

relativePath.description: Root-relative; the service rejects absolute paths and .. segments.

title.description: Titles are drawn as text in the desktop's own faces: a glyph the installed faces lack falls back to another loaded face and then to a small substitution table, so a symbol outside that set draws as a box. Expect the fallback rather than relying on it; a guaranteed symbol needs an icon, not text.

action.description: kind script: script, args, env; kind log: command, filters; kind capture: command, into, format; kind game: game, args (docs/specs/078-project-game-declaration.md). device is available to every kind under contract 4 and defaults to local. stream and operator are reserved for later contracts.

title.description: Titles are drawn as text in the desktop's own faces: a glyph the installed faces lack falls back to another loaded face and then to a small substitution table, so a symbol outside that set draws as a box. Expect the fallback rather than relying on it; a guaranteed symbol needs an icon, not text.

game.description: kind game only: the id of a record in this declaration's games array. A reference to an undeclared id is a named cross-field error.

args.description: kind script: literal argv after the script. kind game: literal argv appended to the referenced record's own args, without ${...} placeholders (enforced as a cross-field rule so script args keep their meaning).

device.description: Contract 4: the id of a device in this declaration's devices array, or the implicit "local". Defaults to "local". A reference to an undeclared id is a named cross-field error, and the key itself requires contract 4.

game.description: One game the workspace launches: literal executable candidates, argv, env, working directory, files that must exist, and how its window is presented. Under contract 4 an optional device says where it runs; for a non-local device the executable and cwd live on that device and are never resolved or stat-ed locally.

id.description: Unique within games; carried on the session as game and used as the gameId selector.

title.description: Toolbar button label with one declared game, menu-entry label with several; the session title is "<title> · <root name>". Titles are drawn as text in the desktop's own faces: a glyph the installed faces lack falls back to another loaded face and then to a small substitution table, so a symbol outside that set draws as a box. Expect the fallback rather than relying on it; a guaranteed symbol needs an icon, not text.

executable.description: Candidates in order; the first that exists and is executable wins. Resolved like a format argv[0].

items.description: A literal argv element; no placeholders.

env.description: Literal variables added over the shell environment. Keys starting RENGINE_, DYLD_ or LD_ are reserved and rejected.

cwd.description: Root-relative working directory for the launched process; "" or an absent key means the project root. No absolute path, no ".." segment, no backslash.

items.description: Root-relative regular file that must exist; each missing one is a named preflight issue.

surface.description: embedded streams the game window into the workspace by injecting the SDL2 adapter into the process; external opens its own operating-system window and only its PTY output is retained; cooperative streams into the same workspace pane from a game that speaks the surface protocol in its own engine, so rEngine reserves the surface and passes RENGINE_SURFACE_PORT/RENGINE_SURFACE_TOKEN but injects nothing. embedded and cooperative both stream into a local pane and are permitted only on the local device (docs/specs/078-project-game-declaration.md).

device.description: Contract 4: the id of a device in this declaration's devices array, or the implicit "local". Defaults to "local". A reference to an undeclared id is a named cross-field error, and the key itself requires contract 4.

value.description: A literal value, such as an ~/.ssh/config host alias.

env.description: An UPPER_SNAKE variable read from the sidecar's shell environment at probe time. Unset or empty is an unreachable device naming the variable, never a spawn with an empty argument.

deviceValue.description: Exactly one of value or env; enforced as a cross-field rule so the message names the record.

probeArgument.description: A literal argv element; the only placeholders are ${host} and ${selector}, and each must have a declared source.

device.description: One place this project's targets run. kind is descriptive: rEngine runs the declared probe and reads its exit status, and holds no ssh or adb knowledge of its own. deviceRequires is reserved for a later contract; requires is always local.

id.description: Unique within devices. "local" is reserved for the kind local device.

title.description: Names the device wherever rEngine shows it. Titles are drawn as text in the desktop's own faces: a glyph the installed faces lack falls back to another loaded face and then to a small substitution table, so a symbol outside that set draws as a box.

host.description: The ssh endpoint, substituted into the probe as ${host}. Not permitted on the local device.

selector.description: Which device, substituted into the probe as ${selector}: an adb serial, or an ssh host alias. Declare it when more than one target can be attached, because a bare adb call aborts with "more than one device" at launch rather than at probe. Not permitted on the local device.

requires.description: Root-relative LOCAL files that must exist, checked before the probe. Local by definition even when the device is remote.

tools.description: Names that must be on the local PATH, checked before the probe.

probe.description: Bounded, side-effect-light argv answering whether this device is reachable right now: exit 0 is reachable, non-zero or timeout is unreachable with the first stderr line as the reason. Run only on an explicit availability check or refresh, never on a timer. Not read-only: adb get-state and adb devices start the adb server when no daemon is running. Reachability is never launchability. Not permitted on the local device.

writeArgument.description: A literal argv element; the only placeholder is ${json}.

agentMenu.description: One agent CLI this project offers: the executable name rEngine launches (claude, codex, gemini, opencode, or an installed executable), the models to choose from, and the one chosen by default. rEngine passes the model with the CLI's own flag and refuses by name for a CLI whose flag it does not know.

id.description: Names this server in diagnostics and in the reason a missing one gives.

command.description: The program and its arguments, run from the project root under the declared-command boundary. rEngine does not install it; a command that is not on the machine is reported as unavailable by name.

match.description: Glob patterns for the files this server serves, matched the way format patterns are.

languageId.description: The protocol's languageId for those files; defaults to the server id.

initializationOptions.description: Passed through to the server's initialize request, unread by rEngine.

pack.description: One pinned, versioned artifact whose facets say how it is consumed (charter D39). A library facet is source and a CMake target a game consumes at build time; a plugin facet is a module the editor loads at run time; one pack may declare both, and the renderer (D30) is expected to. At least one facet is required — a pack with neither is a name and a version with nothing on the other end of them. Where the artifact's bytes come from is deliberately absent from this record: a pack is declared, not acquired.

name.description: The word people say — iklib, rengine-render. Unique within the declaration, and the name a powered-by record and a later edition manifest quote.

pin.description: Two strings that are not interchangeable: a version that is said and a revision that is checked. A version alone is a claim rather than a pin — tags move, and two machines that both say 0.4.0 can hold different bytes — while a revision alone cannot be spoken. A pin declared is not a pin verified: confirming a revision means identifying bytes, which is acquisition and out of this contract's scope.

version.description: The human label a changelog, a powered-by record and an edition manifest quote. Semver is a convention a pack may follow, never a rule this contract imposes: rEngine neither parses nor orders it.

revision.description: The immutable identity: 40 or 64 lowercase hex characters — a git SHA-1 or SHA-256 object id, or a SHA-256 digest of the artifact for a pack that is not a git tree. Which of those it is, is not the manifest's business; the shape is, and the service refuses a branch, a tag or a short prefix by name.

library.description: The BUILD-time facet, and the one D24's "Powered by rEngine" claim is defined on. Source-tree consumption is the only form offered: docs/specs/001-library-pilot.md rules out a nonexistent installed package and an implicit sibling lookup, so a consumer adds the declared directory and links the declared target.

path.description: The directory a consumer adds. Root-relative, refused when it escapes. Its existence is not checked: a pack that has not been fetched is a missing prerequisite, not a malformed declaration.

target.description: The CMake target a game links, such as iklib::ik.

plugin.description: The RUN-time facet: a module the editor loads in process (charter D38). Loading is not in this contract — this block declares what would be loaded.

module.description: The loadable module, root-relative and refused when it escapes. One file: per-platform selection is deliberately a later key rather than a later reinterpretation of this one, so a reader that predates it says "unknown contract" instead of loading the wrong file.

abi.description: An OPAQUE version string. Its shape is checked, so a declaration cannot carry a shell fragment or a kilobyte of prose in it; its meaning belongs to the plugin-ABI lane. rEngine never parses it, never orders two of them, and never refuses one for being too old.
